title: Sand delivered to a construction site

stimulus.title: Sand delivered to a construction site
stimulus.text: Sand is delivered to a construction site at a rate $S(t)$ tons per hour, where $t$ is measured in hours and $0 \le t \le 8$. $S$ is differentiable. Selected values of $S(t)$ are shown in the table. For parts (d) and (e), the rate is modeled by $M(t) = 4 + 3.2\sin\left(\frac{t}{3}\right)$ tons per hour.

table.caption: Rate S(t), in tons per hour, at selected times t, in hours

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use a right Riemann sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table to approximate $\int_0^8 S(t)\,dt$. Show the computations that lead to your answer, and indicate units of measure.

rubric.point: A right Riemann sum with widths 1, 3, 2 and 2

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain the meaning of $\int_0^8 S(t)\,dt$ in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: The total tons of sand delivered to the site from $t = 0$ to $t = 8$ hours
accept: must name the quantity, the units (tons) and the interval

parts.sample: $\int_0^8 S(t)\,dt$ is the total amount of sand, in tons, delivered to the construction site from $t = 0$ to $t = 8$ hours.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Must there be a time $t$, $1 < t < 4$, at which $S(t) = 6$? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Concludes yes by the Intermediate Value Theorem, stating that $S$ is continuous because it is differentiable
accept: "$S$ is differentiable, so it is continuous on $[1, 4]$; by the IVT ..."

parts.sample: $S$ is differentiable, so it is continuous on $[1, 4]$. $S(1) = 5.1 < 6 < 7.1 = S(4)$. By the Intermediate Value Theorem, there is a time $t$ with $1 < t < 4$ at which $S(t) = 6$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Using the model $M$, find the total amount of sand delivered from $t = 0$ to $t = 8$ hours.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Using the model $M$, find the time $T$ at which the total amount of sand delivered since $t = 0$ reaches 25 tons.
parts.sample: Solve $\int_0^T M(t)\,dt = 25$ with the calculator: $T \approx 4.232$ hours. (Since $M(t) > 0$, the total delivered increases, so this is the only such time.)
